notToBeConfusedWith.name: Angostura bark
notToBeConfusedWith.note: The product is named for the Venezuelan town where it was first made, not for the bark; the published account of its own history states the bark is not one of its ingredients.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Orange bitters
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A different, citrus-peel bitters, pale rather than reddish-brown, and not what this drink's aromatic dash is.

forms.label: Standard
forms.animalOriginNote: The producer's own product page states the bitters are 100% vegan and gluten-free.
forms.sourceNote: FoodData Central's branded record for this exact product gives 200 kcal/100 g and 0 g carbohydrate; an independent Open Food Facts entry for the same product agrees on both figures, which is what makes them credible. Neither dataset carries an alcohol figure, because a bottled bitters sold in the US is not required to carry the Nutrition Facts panel that would state one - the 200 kcal/100 g figure is a lab analysis of the food-labelling side only. The 44.7% alc./vol. is the producer's own labelled strength, reported identically by the producer and by every retailer checked. No measured density exists for a bitters this strong with no sugar; the density-classes.json 'spirit-40' class is used as the nearest fit.
